meta.purpose: Published geographic definitions used to resolve an analyst's scope text to airports. Airports are never listed here: membership is always derived from each airport's state code and lat/lon.
sources: U.S. Census Bureau, Census Regions and Divisions of the United States (4 regions, 9 divisions)
metro_aliases: project-defined named areas (center + radius), editable data rows
state_set_aliases: project-defined informal regions (West Coast, Gulf Coast, ...) as explicit state lists with a stated definition; informal names have no official boundary
place names and coordinates are not kept here: they come from the U.S. Census Bureau Gazetteer (data/places.json) and the airports' own reference cities

state_set_aliases.label: West Coast
state_set_aliases.note: West Coast = California, Oregon and Washington, the contiguous states on the Pacific coastline (Alaska and Hawaii also touch the Pacific but are not usually meant).

state_set_aliases.label: East Coast
state_set_aliases.note: East Coast = the 14 states on the Atlantic coastline (ME, NH, MA, RI, CT, NY, NJ, DE, MD, VA, NC, SC, GA, FL) plus the District of Columbia; Pennsylvania has no Atlantic coast and is not included.

state_set_aliases.label: Gulf Coast
state_set_aliases.note: Gulf Coast = Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama and Florida, the five states on the Gulf of Mexico (the whole state is used, not only its coastal part).

state_set_aliases.label: Pacific Northwest
state_set_aliases.note: Pacific Northwest = Washington and Oregon. Idaho is sometimes included and is not here.

state_set_aliases.label: Southwest
state_set_aliases.note: Southwest = Arizona and New Mexico, the core of every definition. Nevada, Texas, Oklahoma, Utah, Colorado and California are sometimes added and are not here.

state_set_aliases.label: Southeast
state_set_aliases.note: Southeast = Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee and Virginia. Arkansas, Louisiana and West Virginia are sometimes added and are not here.

state_set_aliases.label: Mid-Atlantic
state_set_aliases.note: Mid-Atlantic = New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Maryland and the District of Columbia. The Census Bureau's 'Middle Atlantic' division is only NY, NJ and PA, and Virginia and West Virginia are sometimes added.

state_set_aliases.label: Great Lakes states
state_set_aliases.note: Great Lakes states = the eight states that border a Great Lake: Minnesota, Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania and New York (whole states).

state_set_aliases.label: Rocky Mountain states
state_set_aliases.note: Rocky Mountain states = Colorado, Idaho, Montana, Utah and Wyoming. New Mexico and Nevada are sometimes added and are not here.

state_set_aliases.label: Sun Belt
state_set_aliases.note: Sun Belt = a broad southern band: AL, AZ, CA, FL, GA, LA, MS, NV, NM, NC, OK, SC, TX. The term has no official boundary and definitions vary widely.

state_set_aliases.label: Deep South
state_set_aliases.note: Deep South = Alabama, Georgia, Louisiana, Mississippi and South Carolina, the five core states. Texas, Florida and Arkansas are sometimes added and are not here.
